documents.title: UW–Madison Guiding Principles for Generative AI in Teaching
documents.summary: Teaching-center principles for generative AI: equity, data protection, educational uses, assessment redesign, talking with students, and avoiding detectors. It leaves the course rule to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI rule for students; it says "You, as the instructor, might have a policy for the entire course, or you might have specific instructions for individual assignments", so the decision is handed to instructors.

documents.title: Generative AI at UW–Madison: Use Policies
documents.summary: Campus IT use policy for generative AI, mostly on data protection: a table of prohibited uses (protected data, malware, harassment, copyright), human review of AI code, incident reporting and trustworthy-tool advice.
documents.stance_why: It is a conduct and data policy, not a teaching stance; it says what "you may not" do, e.g. "You may not enter any sensitive, restricted or otherwise protected data into any generative AI tool", and permits other uses, so AI is allowed except for listed uses (restrict).
